note: Every entry records its source (B2-R2). Tonewood entries come from the USDA Forest Products Laboratory Wood Handbook, FPL-GTR-282 (2021), read from the PDF; every number is traceable through source.raw, source.derivation and source.locators (printed page and PDF page). Fields the handbook does not provide are null and listed in 'omissions'.

materials.name: sitka_spruce
materials.description: Sitka spruce (Picea sitchensis), softwood grown in the United States (soundboard wood); Table 5-3a.

source.author: Forest Products Laboratory (USDA Forest Service), Madison, WI
source.title: Wood handbook - wood as an engineering material, General Technical Report FPL-GTR-282 (March 2021)
source.locator: Row 'Spruce, Sitka': Table 5-3a (metric), printed p. 5-8, PDF p. 124; Table 5-1 (printed p. 5-2, PDF p. 118); Table 5-2 (printed p. 5-3, PDF p. 119); Chapter 4 Eqs. 4-9, 4-11, 4-14; Chapter 5 Eq. 5-3. Per-field locators in source.locators.
source.licence: Public domain (work of the United States government, 17 U.S.C. 105); no restriction on reuse or redistribution of the numbers.

derivation.youngsL: E_L = 1.10 x E_bending(12 %) = 1.10 x 10800 MPa = 11880 MPa = 1.188e+10 Pa. E_bending(12 %) = 10800 MPa from Table 5-3a (metric), printed p. 5-8, PDF p. 124, row Spruce, Sitka, 12 % line, modulus of elasticity. The tabulated value is a static-bending modulus that includes shear deflection; the 1.10 factor is the handbook's own correction (Table 5-3a footnote c, printed p. 5-8: 'To correct for shear deflection, the modulus can be increased by 10%'; Table 5-1 footnote a, printed p. 5-2, PDF p. 118: 'EL may be approximated by increasing modulus of elasticity values in Table 5-3 by 10%'; text on printed p. 5-2: 'EL from bending can be increased by 10% to remove this effect approximately'). For Table 5-5a species the handbook states no span/depth ratio; the same 10 % rule of the text is applied.
derivation.youngsR: E_R = (E_R/E_L) x E_L = 0.078 x 11880 MPa = 926.64 MPa = 9.2664e+08 Pa; E_R/E_L = 0.078 from Table 5-1 (printed p. 5-2, PDF p. 118); applied to the shear-corrected E_L as the handbook directs (printed p. 5-2: 'This adjusted bending EL can be used to determine ER and ET based on the ratios in Table 5-1').
derivation.shearLR: G_LR = (G_LR/E_L) x E_L = 0.064 x 11880 MPa = 760.32 MPa = 7.6032e+08 Pa; G_LR/E_L = 0.064 from Table 5-1 (printed p. 5-2, PDF p. 118), same shear-corrected E_L.
derivation.poissonLR: nu_LR = 0.372 from Table 5-2 (printed p. 5-3, PDF p. 119), column muLR.
derivation.poissonRL: nu_RL = 0.04 from Table 5-2 (printed p. 5-3, PDF p. 119), column muRL.
derivation.density: Tabulated G12 = 0.4 (Table 5-3a (metric), printed p. 5-8, PDF p. 124, row Spruce, Sitka, 12 % line; footnote b: ovendry mass, volume at 12 % MC). rho12 = 1000 kg/m^3 x G12 x (1 + 12/100) = 448 kg/m^3 (Eq. 4-14 with x = 12; Table 4-5: rho12 is mass and volume both at 12 % MC).
derivation.lossFactor: Not available. The handbook gives no species value of internal friction or loss factor. Its only statement (Chapter 5, internal friction, printed p. 5-21, PDF p. 137) is that 'the value of internal friction, expressed by logarithmic decrement, ranges from about 0.1 for hot, moist wood to less than 0.02 for hot, dry wood', with cool wood intermediate. That is a range over temperature and moisture, not a value for this species at 12 % MC and room temperature, so no number is recorded (constants.lossFactor is null). The caller must supply the loss factor to library.apply.

moistureSlopes.dEdMcL: Eq. 5-3 (printed p. 5-34, PDF p. 150): P(M) = P12 (P12/Pg)^((12 - M)/(Mp - 12)), M in %. P12 = 10800 MPa and Pg = 8500 MPa (green line) from Table 5-3a (metric), printed p. 5-8, PDF p. 124, row Spruce, Sitka; Mp = 27 % (Table 5-13 (printed p. 5-34, PDF p. 150) row Spruce, Sitka). Derivative at M = 12: dP/dM = -P12 ln(P12/Pg)/(Mp - 12) = -10800 x ln(10800/8500)/(27 - 12) = -172.426 MPa per % MC. Times the 1.10 shear correction of E_L: -189.668 MPa per % MC = -1.89668e+10 Pa per unit MC fraction (x 100 for % to fraction, x 1e6 for MPa to Pa). The handbook excludes work to maximum load, impact bending and tension perpendicular from Eq. 5-3; the modulus of elasticity is not excluded.
moistureSlopes.dEdMcR: Not available. The handbook gives E_R/E_L only at about 12 % MC (Table 5-1) and no green values or moisture adjustment for E_R, so no slope is derived; stored as null (applied as 0). Scaling E_R with the E_L slope would be an assumption the handbook does not make.
moistureSlopes.dGdMc: Not available. The handbook gives G_LR/E_L only at about 12 % MC (Table 5-1) and no moisture adjustment for G_LR; stored as null (applied as 0).
moistureSlopes.dRhodMc: rho(M) = 1000 x Gb x (1 + M/100)/(1 - S0/100 (1 - M/30)) from Eq. 4-14 with Gx = Gb/(1 - Sx/100) (Eq. 4-11) and Sx = S0 (1 - M/MCfs), MCfs = 30 % (Eq. 4-9), M <= 30. Gb = 0.37 (Table 5-3a (metric), printed p. 5-8, PDF p. 124), S0 = 11.5 % (Table 4-3 (printed p. 4-8, PDF p. 102) row Spruce, Sitka (volumetric)). Derivative at M = 12: u = 1 - S0/100 (1 - 12/30) = 0.931000; du/dM = S0/(100 x 30) = 0.00383333; d(rho)/dM = 1000 Gb [u/100 - (1 + 12/100) du/dM]/u^2 = 2.1415 kg/m^3 per % MC = 214.15 kg/m^3 per unit MC fraction.

locators.youngsR: Table 5-1 (printed p. 5-2, PDF p. 118); E_L as above

locators.density: Table 5-3a (metric), printed p. 5-8, PDF p. 124 (specific gravity); Chapter 4 Eqs. 4-9, 4-11, 4-14 (printed pp. 4-10 to 4-12, PDF pp. 104-106); Table 4-3 (printed p. 4-8, PDF p. 102) row Spruce, Sitka (volumetric)

locators.dEdMcL: Eq. 5-3, printed p. 5-34, PDF p. 150; Mp: Table 5-13 (printed p. 5-34, PDF p. 150) row Spruce, Sitka; Table 5-3a (metric), printed p. 5-8, PDF p. 124 (green and 12 % MOE)

omissions: Norway (European) spruce (Picea abies): not in the handbook's property tables (Tables 5-1 to 5-5, 4-3, 4-4 have no Picea abies row; it appears only in text and references). Not included.

Not included.
Ebony (Diospyros spp.): Table 4-4 has shrinkage only; no stiffness, density or elastic ratios in Tables 5-1 to 5-5. Not included (optional in the card).
Bigleaf maple: Table 5-3a has bending properties but Tables 5-1 and 5-2 have no bigleaf row; sugar maple (complete in all tables) is the maple entry. Red maple has elastic ratios but was not added.

Loss factor eta, all tonewood entries: the handbook gives no species value, only a range of the logarithmic decrement (about 0.1 for hot moist wood to less than 0.02 for hot dry wood, printed p. 5-21, PDF p. 137). constants.lossFactor is null; library.apply requires a loss_factor argument.
